---
title: "Guarantees and limits"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Guarantees and limits}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---


A successful in-memory trial proves that its retained input passed the configured
checks. It does not reserve a future source version or promise that a later run
will see the same external data. Definition construction does not read or write
sources. Execution can do both.

Lake releases preserve published versions during ordinary publication. Publication
coordinates registry state and storage, but a process crash can leave intermediate
objects. Inspect interrupted runs and use the lake recovery and cleanup functions
before retrying. Do not assume an external target adapter provides the same
transaction or recovery guarantees as a managed lake.

Local lake writes require one coordinated writer. Do not run independent local
writers against the same catalog. Shared writers require the supported PostgreSQL
coordination configuration; using an object store alone does not provide locking.
The PostgreSQL integration job exercises separate writer processes. Backend and
crash behavior still require testing against the deployment configuration.

Writer bookkeeping is process-local and keyed to the connection configuration.
A future or targets worker must open its own resources and close those it owns.
Do not serialize live database connections into workers. Definitions are ordinary
R values; closures supplied by users can themselves capture mutable state.

“Immutable” describes normal release publication, not a legal retention policy or
undeletable storage. Operators must define retention for data, registry metadata,
quality evidence, frozen reports, backups and downstream catalogs. Deleting one
release does not erase its copies. Resolve deletion requests across those stores;
DataRaft does not provide a universal subject-erasure operation.
